issues.failure_explanation: Assumption 1 controls the generator only in time-integrated form and up to time-null sets. It does not imply that the sampled F_i are square-integrable. For T=1, xi=0 and f(t,omega,y,z)=1_{t=1} exp(B_1(omega)^2), all its conditions hold, but F_m=Delta_m exp(B_1^2) is not even integrable. Thus the martingale representation and chaos coefficients cannot be constructed. Likewise, the stated almost-everywhere Lipschitz condition need not hold at the grid nodes used in the stability proofs.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require square-integrability of f(t_i,0,0) and the stated Lipschitz bound almost surely at every evaluated node, or explicitly choose a representative having these properties. Then prove square-integrability by backward induction.
issues.overall_effect: The recursion and its implementation estimates are not guaranteed to be well defined under the stated BSDE data assumptions.
issues.title: The Euler recursion lacks admissibility conditions at the sampled times
issues.why_classification: This is a local grid-admissibility repair. Values at finitely many times can be specified without changing the BSDE, and the algorithm and rates under their respective regularity hypotheses need not change.

issues.failure_explanation: Take d=1, k=1, P>=1 and F=B(h_{M+1}), where h_{M+1} is orthogonal to the retained basis. The left side is zero, whereas the right side equals the nonzero deterministic function h_{M+1}(s). Finite-basis truncation must also project the Malliavin time-direction variables; truncating only the random-variable chaos is insufficient.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Let Q_M be the orthogonal projection onto the retained deterministic basis and replace the identity by D^k C^{P,M}F = Q_M^{tensor k} C^{P-k,M}(D^k F). Use its integrated norm contraction where needed.
issues.overall_effect: The finite-basis identity in part (ii) is false. The full-chaos identity and the integrated derivative-norm contraction needed later remain available.
issues.title: Malliavin differentiation does not commute with finite-basis truncation as claimed
issues.why_classification: The correction follows locally from the paper's kernel-projection representation and preserves the subsequent norm estimates and convergence rates.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We emphasize the fact that the method can be implemented in the case of a random generator $f$.

issues.failure_explanation: The construction supplies Brownian replicas but no corresponding copies of the random field f. As written, every summand uses the original random generator. For xi=0 and f(t,omega,y,z)=B_t(omega), the final-step constant coefficient is hat d_0^m=Delta_m B_T. It is not measurable with respect to the auxiliary sigma-field F^{m<=}. Consequently, the conditional-expectation formulas cannot treat the estimated coefficients as fixed, and the claimed random-generator implementation fails.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Construct generator replicas jointly with each simulation Brownian motion and evaluate f^{i,n} in the corresponding summand. Establish their conditional sampling and measurability properties before applying the closed-form formulas.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised implementation for random generators lacks the sampling and independence structure required by its formulas. The explicitly deterministic convergence analysis is not affected by this particular defect.
issues.title: The Monte Carlo recursion does not resample a random generator
issues.why_classification: Preserving the advertised random-generator capability requires a contained additional sampling construction, rather than merely changing a constant or notation.

issues.failure_explanation: Summing the recursion leaves I_m-I_0; the positive terminal term I_m cannot be discarded. Also, the explicitly added integrals cover [t_1,T], not [0,T]. Writing R for the weighted sum of projection residuals, the justified bound is total Z-error <= 2 I_m + 2C sum_i Delta_i I_i + 4R, using I_0 to control the first interval. The displayed bound without I_m can fail for a terminal projection error whose martingale energy is concentrated near T.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Perform the telescoping with the actual interval range, retain 2 I_m, and then apply the already proved maximum-I estimate.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed derivation of the integrated Z-error estimate is invalid, although the stated lemma can retain its current bound.
issues.title: The implementation-error proof drops a terminal energy boundary term
issues.why_classification: Correct boundary bookkeeping and the existing Gronwall bound complete the proof without changing its conclusion, assumptions, or rate.

issues.failure_explanation: The implemented recursion has Delta_i C^P(f_i) on its right-hand side, not Delta_i f_i. For a nonlinear generator these differ, so the equation being differentiated and the resulting differentiated equality are false. The omission cannot be justified by finite-dimensional measurability: that removes basis truncation, not truncation of chaos order.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Differentiate the projected recursion. Its differentiated right-hand side is C^{P-1}(D_s Y_{t_i}+Delta_i D_s f_i); use the valid full-chaos commutation identity and L2 contraction to recover the subsequent energy inequality.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the uniform Malliavin energy bound, and hence the supplied proof of the order-truncation error rate, has a gap.
issues.title: The Malliavin energy proof differentiates the wrong recursion
issues.why_classification: A local projection-contraction argument using results already in the paper restores the same energy estimates and rates.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let Assumption \ref{main assumption convergence rate} be satisfied.

issues.failure_explanation: The standing assumption is only Assumption 1, whereas the invoked Euler rate requires the substantially stronger regularity assumption stated earlier. A concrete counterexample is T=1, xi=0 and f(t,y,z)=1_Q(t). This bounded, deterministic generator satisfies Assumption 1 and is Lipschitz at every time. The true solution is zero, but on uniform rational grids the exact-coefficient scheme gives Y_0^{pi,theta}=1 for every P and M. The asserted right side is C/m, so both bounds fail. Assumption 1 also does not ensure that D xi appearing in the estimate exists.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Impose the existing main convergence-rate assumption, the required Malliavin domains, and the small-mesh restrictions when stating the main estimates. Any retained claim for the full Assumption 1 regime needs a different convergence argument and an appropriately weaker error statement.
issues.overall_effect: Neither main theorem establishes its advertised time-discretization rate under the stated assumptions, and the derivative-based bounds do not cover arbitrary square-integrable terminal conditions.
issues.title: The main convergence estimates are asserted under insufficient regularity assumptions
issues.why_classification: The source-supported repair excludes the advertised unrestricted square-integrable/measurable-data regime. Preserving that regime and the stated rates is impossible for the given counterexample.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Under Assumption \ref{assumption 1}, the random variable $\xi$ has absolute moments of fourth order, and hence $\mathbf{V}_{m}(\xi)$ can be proven to be finite.

issues.failure_explanation: Assumption 1 gives only L2 integrability, not fourth moments or finite weighted coefficient variances. Let T=1, G=B_1, f=0 and xi=exp(G^2/4)/(1+G^2). Then xi and its first Malliavin derivative are square-integrable, but E[xi^2 H_2(G)^2]=infinity. For P=2 and M=1, V_m(xi) is infinite and the terminal Monte Carlo chaos estimate has infinite mean-square error for every N. This occurs already at initialization, independently of time-discretization error. The displayed estimate is therefore at best an infinite, vacuous bound, not the claimed finite Monte Carlo convergence guarantee.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $\Sigma_{ij}=\sigma^{i}L_{ij}$, where $L$ denotes the lower triangular matrix in the Cholesky decomposition $C = L L^{T}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper's hedge relation gives diag(S_t)H_t=Sigma^{-T}Z_t. Hence the amount invested in risky assets is 1^T Sigma^{-T}Z_t, and the cash balance entering the borrowing term must be y-1^T Sigma^{-T}z. The driver instead uses Sigma^{-1}. These differ for the specified nonsymmetric Cholesky volatility matrix. Thus the stated BSDE is not the claimed borrowing/lending pricing problem.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace Sigma^{-1} by Sigma^{-T} in the cash-balance term and recompute or validate the numerical outputs for that driver. Alternatively, present the existing experiment solely as an abstract five-dimensional BSDE test.
issues.overall_effect: The financial interpretation of Example 3's reported prices and hedging trajectories is not established for the specified asset model.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $(\xi^{1}, \dots, \xi^{N})$ an $N$-dimensional copy of $\xi$, with $\xi^{n}$ being $\mathcal{F}_{T}^{\xi, n}$-measurable;

where in the last equality we used the i.i.d. assumption
on $(B^{\xi, n})_{n}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The stated sampling conditions specify marginal copies of xi but not copies of its joint law with the Brownian path. Take T=P=M=1, xi=B_1 and xi^n=-B_1^{xi,n}. These are independent copies of xi with exactly the required measurability. Nevertheless, the estimated first-chaos coefficient converges to -1 instead of 1. Directly, the left side of the claimed identity is 4+3/N, whereas V_m(xi)/N=3/N. Independence of the Brownian replicas alone does not justify the centering used in the proof.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require the pairs (xi^n,B^{xi,n}) to be independent copies of (xi,B), for example by evaluating the same measurable Wiener functional defining xi on every replica.
issues.overall_effect: The terminal coefficient estimator can be biased under the stated sampling specification, invalidating the Monte Carlo error identities and resulting convergence guarantee.
issues.title: Marginal copies of the terminal variable do not ensure unbiased chaos coefficients
issues.why_classification: A standard local joint-sampling condition repairs the unbiasedness argument without restricting the terminal laws or changing the method and rates.
